QUOTE: "By default it expands to `private_##member`, so a field such as `mbedtls_aes_context::MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(nr)` ... is declared as `private_nr`. Code that writes `ctx.nr` then fails to compile. The struct layout and the header stay the same, but the names are hidden from ordinary callers. The header is not an encapsulation boundary at runtime; it is a compile-time guard on the field names."
VERDICT: HIT
WHY: The answer says the member name is renamed so access fails at compile time, while the struct layout stays unchanged.
